newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thai Airways to lift ex-Paris cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways to lift ex-Paris cargo rates.

text.p: Thai airways said it planned to increase its ex-Paris cargo rates, effective March 1.

"With a few exceptions, notably Australia, the increases will be across-the-board and vary between five and seven percent depending on the destination," a Paris-based Thai cargo official told Reuters.
Thai operates a twice-weekly 747-200 full-freighter service between Paris and Bangkok, in conjunction with Air France.
The Thai carrier also operates a daily 747 passenger service on the same route.
Thai last increased its ex-Paris cargo rates during the 1995/1996 winter season.

"In terms of cargo activity, last month for us was much more buoyant than January 1996 and overall, the market outlook for 1997 is positive," the official said, adding: "The impact of a strengthening dollar has yet to be really felt in France in comparison to other European countries but clearly this will serve to boost export traffic."
Economic growth forecasts for Thailand in 1997 had been revised recently from seven to eight percent which would probably act as a spur on export traffic too, the official said.
